title: I am very disappointed with this steamer; design is poor-- it has too many parts – 2.5 stars
text:
I am very disappointed with this steamer; design is poor-- it has too many parts – 2.5 stars. I am a steamer fanatic who mostly cooks everything with steam; this is my 15th steamer! Unfortunately, this is not even worth the money I have to lay out for this, in my opinion.

I have been steaming most of my meals for about 30 years. In those 30 years, I owned or previously owned 14 steamers. This is my 15th steamer and it is a whopping disappointment. I put this through the paces and it is one of my least favorite steamers. Yes it works, but it is cumbersome and bulky and has too many moving parts.

WHAT is in the BOX - In addition to the instruction manual, this comes in 11 parts as follows:

- Base unit
- Heater cap (also known as steam guard)
- Three (3) steam tray bottoms
- Three (3) steaming basket "rims" (upper, middle, and lower or what I call small, medium, and large)
- Top lid
- Rice bowl
- Drip Tray

FEATURES
- The steaming controls are LED and it comes with preset times for eggs, rice, fish, chicken/meat, and vegetables. I do not need this but newbies might like it.

- There is a keep-warm function (it is unclear for how long) and a timer function that allows steaming to be delayed anywhere from 1 minute to 12 hours and 59 minutes. I tested both the timer and keep-warm feature and they work well.

- The baskets are an opaque plastic and each basket is two loose pieces.

- The steamer has boil-dry protection so that it turns off if the reservoir is out of water.

LIKES
- The steamer cooks almost equally with all three baskets simultaneously. I usually put the food that gets done the quickest (the most delicate foods like fish) on top away from the intensity of the steam. The uppermost basket does not cook as fast but this is expected.

- It can steam a lot of food since it has three vertical levels.

- I can steam 18 eggs at one time--six in each basket. When I steam eggs, I want them to steam the same. I tested this and the eggs steamed in the top basket were less cooked than those in the bottom basket. However, this is to be expected. Note that I leave the uncooked eggs on the counter for about one hour before steaming so that they do not break during cooking.

- The keep-warm and delay-start features are nice to have.

- When in operation, the steamer is relatively quiet until the food is ready; that is when the beeps sound.

- A full reservoir provides enough steam for at least 60 minutes of steaming which is very generous; most steamers only last 45 minutes on full.

- Descaling is easy just like it is for all the other steamers I own. This steamer will develop mineral build up on the heating element. All that has to be done is to fill the reservoir with equal parts vinegar and water and heat on high for twenty minutes. I actually use almost 100% vinegar in most of my steamers. I have not used this long enough yet to implement descaling.

DISLIKES
- The opaqueness of the baskets makes it difficult to see how the food is doing during steaming.

- Each basket comes in two pieces. It is also easy to have the bottom slip out if not seated correctly. In addition, the top has to be placed on the uppermost basket just right or that will slip off too.

- The LED is awkward in the sense that the on/off button has to be pressed more than once to start the steaming process. I kept thinking the steaming would start and then the unit would turn off. The only way I could tell I got it right was when the two dots (:) blinked.

- There are way too many moving parts. The design of the baskets is very poor. They come apart like a springform pan without the spring.

- The unit with the baskets is also big and bulky and does not collapse into a small enough footprint for storage.

- There is no reservoir refill hole on the outside of the steamer. If I were serial steaming various foods, I would run out of water and would have to handle a hot steamer to refill or wait until it cools. When there is an outside hole for the reservoir, I can use a teapot or something with a spout to refill the steamer during operation or between operations without getting burned. Since the reservoir holds about 60 minutes of water, this issue will not affect me much as I rarely do more than two steaming sessions that go beyond one hour.

- Although this does not affect me at all, beware that the steamer is tall when in use. In addition, the cord is short as is expected of any appliance such as this.

In summary, I am utterly disappointed in this steamer. Although it works, it is cumbersome to use, too bulky, and has too many pieces. The design is not well-thought out. My main disappointment is that each basket is two pieces (a flat removable bottom and a plastic ring for the sided), which makes absolutely no sense to me.

For those who are interested, here are MY STEAMERS - PAST and PRESENT

PAST 3 STEAMERS that eventually broke:

- One small round Black and Decker Steamer (extinct now) which was great and super small but only lasted about two years. This was my first steamer that I purchased in the 1990's.

- One [[ASIN:B00004SPEI Krups Optisteam Plus]]. I had this since February 1999 and it was my most used steamer and very similar to the Oster steamer.

- One [[ASIN:B00073HLMU Oster 5711 Mechanical Food Steamer]], which I used daily for my oatmeal and most dinners until it died.

CURRENT 12 STEAMERS (counts one that I have three of):

- This one [[ASIN:B07ZFKMVL3 AmazonBasics 12.5 Quart 3-Tiered Digital Food Steamer]]. The basket design is poor and it is too bulky. I would pass.

- This [[ASIN:B07H79RGVJ Secura Electric Food Steamer]]. This is my favorite steamer. No plastic comes in contact with the food. It has few moving parts and steams evenly and well. If I had the room, I would buy a second one because, as of this writing, I cannot bear the thought of being without it.

- One [[ASIN:B01MZF7ZFZ Breville Steam Zone steamer]] – this one is large; has an annoying ticking noise during operation and cooks unevenly. The option of using only the steaming tray w/o the pots allows for cooking large items like fillets of fish. I rarely use this steamer due to its lackluster functionality.

- One [[ASIN:B008FX6KH6 T-fal VC133851 Balanced Living Compact Electric Food Steamer, 4-Quart, Silver]] – this one is too small, is discontinued, and its steam is not hot enough requiring longer cooking times. I use this one occasionally for rolled oats or some vegetables.

- One [[ASIN:B00019G8IS Oster 5712 Electronic Food Steamer]] - I use this daily for my oatmeal and most dinners. This is still my GOTO steamer in addition to my Secura. This steamer will fail soon as I have had it almost six years and they usually do not last more than that before it burns out. This steamer also appears to be discontinued which is why a once $30 steamer is now being sold for almost $275.

- Three [[ASIN:B000JJMER4 Richard Simmons EST7 Steam-Heat Electronic Food Steamers]] which I absolutely love. These are very large steamers and are larger than the Breville. They have three steaming chambers and are good for steaming full meals (protein, starch, and vegetable) that FINISH at the same time by counting down in reverse. This remains my other GOTO steamer. This is the type of steamer that is not for everyone and which is why it was discontinued due to lack of customer interest. Because I love it so much, I purchased three as I cannot bear to be without one even though I do not use it daily.

- One rice steamer, the [[ASIN:B00007J5U7 Zojirushi NS-ZCC10 5-1/2-Cup Neuro Fuzzy Rice Cooker and Warmer, Premium White]], which is excellent but which I do not use nearly enough. It is also a little different that these other steamers in function so they really cannot be compared.

- One [[ASIN:B003NTXFVG Hard Anodized Non-Stick Wok with Steamer and Lid]]. In addition to this, I also have another very small pot with a steamer on top but I am not counting this one.

- One Stove-top fish steamer similar to the [[ASIN:B0002IBJG4 Norpro Stainless Steel Fish Poacher]].

- One asparagus steamer very similar to [[ASIN:B079DD9115 this one]].

UPDATE: I forgot to attach a picture of the two piece baskets so I am attaching it now.

features: 8.5-quart 2-tiered stackable food steamer uses the power of steam to cook food to perfection; design allows for steam-cooking larger quantities or 2 different types of food at the same time

Control panel with digital display for easily adjusting the cooking time and temperature; water-level indicator for convenient filling; an audible signal indicates the end of the cooking cycle; keep-warm mode
Made of durable BPA-free plastic; parts nest together for compact storage; includes a 1.5-liter rice bowl
Dishwasher-safe rice bowl and drip tray; food containers should be hand-washed in warm, soapy water
Black and stainless-steel housing with cord storage for a sleek appearance; 750 watts of power; backed by an Amazon Basics 1-year limited warranty
